questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Sable Footwear Co, a national firm wraps its Stonebridge product in green packaging and labels it "earth friendly" while making no change to an energy-intensive production process. What is the most accurate description?
questions.explanation: Greenwashing is presenting a product or company as environmentally responsible when the underlying practice does not support the claim. Here the packaging and label imply environmental benefit while production remains energy-intensive, which misleads consumers. Genuine sustainable marketing requires real changes to processes and products, backed by credible evidence, not just a green label.

questions.stem: Brightwater Packaging, a small firm tracks Fairhaven customers' online behaviour and builds detailed profiles without telling them or offering a way to opt out. Which ethical principle is most directly violated?
questions.explanation: Collecting detailed behavioural data without disclosure or consent violates consumer privacy and the principle of informed consent. People should know what is being collected and have meaningful control over it. Cost, brand awareness and competition do not excuse hidden data collection, which can also breach data-protection laws.
